title: RTL-Repair: Fast Symbolic Repair of Hardware Design Code
problem: Register transfer level (RTL) circuit descriptions contain bugs that existing repair tools fix very slowly, requiring minutes to hours. Developers need fast, automated repair suggestions to improve hardware design productivity.
motivation: Integrating fast repair tools into IDEs enables developers to receive repair suggestions promptly, significantly improving hardware design workflows.
method: RTL-Repair uses an SMT-based one-step fault localization and repair algorithm with optimization to generate minimal code changes. An adaptive windowing approach focuses the repair search on the most relevant parts of test cases, avoiding scalability bottlenecks of previous methods.
key_novelty: Adaptive windowing technique that focuses fault localization and repair on the most relevant test portions to achieve sub-second repair times while maintaining solution quality.
contributions: SMT-based one-step joint fault localization and repair algorithm for RTL designs
Adaptive windowing approach to focus repair search and achieve scalability
Evaluation on 12 real bugs from open-source hardware projects achieving 75% fix rate
Generation of minimal, human-interpretable repairs suitable for IDE integration

metrics.speedup: seconds vs minutes/hours compared to previous state-of-the-art
metrics.accuracy: 9/12 bugs produce passing repairs (75%); 2 fully correct, 1 partial, 4 overfit testbench, 3 incorrect

limitations: Only 75% of bugs produce testbench-passing repairs; some repairs overfit to test cases rather than matching ground truth.
primary_theme: Fast symbolic repair of hardware designs
